1. edge/defaults.toml - baseline for every binding

initial_files.README.md:
# topup-gateway workspace

topup-gateway forwards prepaid wallet top-ups to the card issuer. E_TOPUP_FAILED
marks a top-up the issuer refused or that timed out before settlement.

Application logs live under logs/; logs/topup-gateway.log is a single rolling
file that holds several days. Every line starts with a UTC timestamp carrying a
Z suffix.

Our forwarder retries a failed top-up and the issuer also re-sends its own
callback, so one top-up can produce several E_TOPUP_FAILED lines. Every retry
and re-delivery carries the same payment reference (the ref= token).

# scan-station-relay workspace

scan-station-relay forwards barcode scans from the parcel sorters to the
warehouse service. E_BARCODE_UNREADABLE marks a scan whose label could not be
decoded, so the parcel was diverted to manual handling.

Application logs live under logs/ and rotate by UTC date: every closed segment
is kept as logs/scan-station-relay.log.<YYYY-MM-DD> named after the UTC day it
covers, and logs/scan-station-relay.log is the current, still-open segment. One
local reporting day usually spans two segments.

Every line starts with a UTC timestamp carrying a Z suffix, then the level,
then the service name in brackets. The line team reviews scans by its own fixed
UTC-3 reporting day.

identity-fanout pushes consent changes to downstream services. E_CONSENT_DROP

Two services take part in stream ingest:

- ingest-scheduler assigns event-stream partitions to ingest workers. Plain-text

attempt for the same batch keeps the same job id (the job= token).

initial_files.README.md:
Harbourline Community Workshop - hire desk
=========================================

The booking vendor migrated the nightly equipment-hire export in
September and renamed every key in the JSON. The scheduler runs the
feed script from a scratch directory, so it must always find its
exports from the directory it is launched in, never from the script's
own folder.

hire_feed_layout.md is the layout the front desk and the noticeboard
screen both read from.
initial_files.hire_feed_layout.md:
Hire feed layout - workshop ops, v3 (2026-09-14)
================================================

The nightly hire feed is printed to standard output:

  hire_ref,member_code,item_code,due_on

The September export renamed every record key:

  ref        -> hire_ref
  member     -> member_code
  item       -> item_code
  due        -> due_on
  span_days  is workshop-internal and never printed

The records of an export live under its top-level "bookings" array.
Every hires-*.json export under the launch directory is swept,
wherever an export sits.

Ordering of the data lines:
  - hires are listed by due_on ascending, earliest first;
  - hires sharing a due_on are listed by hire_ref ascending;
  - a hire that is not scheduled yet carries an empty "due" value;
    unscheduled hires follow every scheduled hire, again ordered by
    hire_ref ascending.

The feed carries exactly one line per hire and every value is
copied through unchanged. No value ever contains a comma.

"""Nightly hire feed for the Harbourline Community Workshop.

Prints the hire feed to standard output.
"""
import json
from pathlib import Path

BASE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
EXPORT = BASE / "hires-2026-09-14.json"


def main() -> None:
    export = json.loads(EXPORT.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    print("hire_ref,member_code,item_code,due_on")
    for record in export.get("hires", []):
        print(",".join([
            record["hire_id"],
            record["member_code"],
            record["item_code"],
            record["due_on"],
        ]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Nightly hire feed for the Harbourline Community Workshop.

Sweeps the launch directory for hires-*.json exports and prints the
feed to stdout.
"""
import glob
import json
import os


def main() -> None:
    rows = []
    pattern = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "**", "hires-*.json")
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(pattern, recursive=True)):
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            export = json.load(handle)
        for record in export.get("bookings", []):
            rows.append((
                record.get("ref", ""),
                record.get("member", ""),
                record.get("item", ""),
                record.get("due", ""),
            ))
    rows.sort(key=lambda row: (row[3] == "", row[3], row[0]))
    print("hire_ref,member_code,item_code,due_on")
    for row in rows:
        print(",".join(row))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Wardley Seed Bank - intake vault
================================

`python3 intake_summary.py` with the vault directory as its working

initial_files.intake_rules.md:
Seed intake summary - accession rules, v2 (2026-09-30)
=====================================================

The summary is printed to standard output:

  species_code,total_packets
  ... one line per listed species ...

An intake export carries a top-level "intake" array. Each record is:

  species   the species code, e.g. SP-BIRCH
  packets   whole packets in this accession
  state     stored, returned or discarded

How packets count towards a species total:
  - state=stored adds its packets to the species total;
  - state=returned subtracts its packets from the species total;
  - state=discarded never counts at all, neither way.

Which species are listed:
  - only species whose total_packets reaches the storage threshold
    of 100 packets or more; a species exactly at 100 is listed, and
    a species below 100 is left out.

Ordering of the species lines:
  - species are listed by total_packets descending, largest first;
  - species sharing a total are listed by species_code ascending.

Exports are collected from every intake-*.json file under the launch
directory, no matter which folder an export sits in.

"""Nightly dispensary batch sheet for Grove End Pharmacy.

Sweeps the packing area for batches-*.csv exports and prints the
nightly sheet to standard output.
"""
import csv
import glob
import os


def main() -> None:
    pattern = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "**", "batches-*.csv")
    rows = []
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(pattern, recursive=True)):
        with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            rows.extend(csv.DictReader(handle))
    rows.sort(key=lambda row: (row["priority"] != "yes",
                               row["carrier_service"],
                               row["order_id"]))
    print("batch_ref,station_code,item_count,rush_flag")
    for row in rows:
        print(",".join([row["batch_ref"], row["station_code"],
                        row["item_count"], row["rush_flag"]]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Nightly dispensary batch sheet for Grove End Pharmacy.

Sweeps the packing area for batches-*.csv exports and prints the
nightly sheet to standard output.
"""
import csv
import glob
import os


def main() -> None:
    pattern = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "**", "batches-*.csv")
    rows = []
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(pattern, recursive=True)):
        with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            rows.extend(csv.DictReader(handle))
    listed = [row for row in rows if int(row["item_count"]) > 0]
    listed.sort(key=lambda row: (row["station_code"] == "",
                                 row["station_code"],
                                 row["rush_flag"] != "yes",
                                 row["batch_ref"]))
    print("batch_ref,station_code,item_count,rush_flag")
    for row in listed:
        print(",".join([row["batch_ref"], row["station_code"],
                        row["item_count"], row["rush_flag"]]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

initial_files.load_rules.md:
Dock load counter - Wexcombe Print Works, rules v3 (2026-09-18)
==============================================================

The counter is printed to standard output:

  dock_code,load
  ... one line per listed dock ...

A ticket export carries, in this order:

  ticket_ref, dock_code, carrier, state

state is issued, reissued or void. A reissued ticket is the same
ticket sent to the dock a second time, not a second ticket, and a
ticket never changes dock once it has been exported.

How a dock's load is counted:
  - a ticket_ref that appears at least once with state=void was
    cancelled and counts for no dock at all, whatever else was
    exported for it;
  - every other ticket_ref counts once towards the dock recorded on
    its rows, however many times it was exported.

Which docks are listed:
  - a dock is listed only when its load is at least 1; a dock whose
    every ticket was voided is left out.

Ordering of the dock lines:
  - docks are listed by load descending, busiest dock first;
  - docks sharing a load are listed by dock_code ascending.

Exports are collected from every tickets-*.csv file under the launch
directory, no matter which folder an export sits in. carrier is for
the print room only and is never printed.

arguments.content:
"""Dock load counter for Wexcombe Print Works.

Sweeps the launch directory for tickets-*.csv exports and prints
the per-dock load to standard output.
"""
import csv
import glob
import os


def main() -> None:
    pattern = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "**", "tickets-*.csv")
    rows = []
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(pattern, recursive=True)):
        with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            rows.extend(csv.DictReader(handle))
    voided = {row["ticket_ref"] for row in rows if row["state"] == "void"}
    loads = {}
    for row in rows:
        ref = row["ticket_ref"]
        if ref in voided:
            continue
        loads.setdefault(row["dock_code"], set()).add(ref)
    listed = [(dock, len(refs)) for dock, refs in loads.items() if refs]
    listed.sort(key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0]))
    print("dock_code,load")
    for dock, load in listed:
        print("%s,%d" % (dock, load))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

initial_files.README.md:
Beacon Hill Observatory - dome session log
=========================================

The scheduler launches the report as `python3 dome_report.py` from
a scratch directory, never from the log folder itself, so the
report has to sweep the archived exports wherever they sit.

The log vendor migrated the export layout on 2026-09-01. Before
the migration an export was:

  account_id, signed_in_at, status

The new layout puts the timestamp first, adds the observer and
dome columns, and appends a free-text note whose values may contain
commas (double-quoted, standard CSV):

  logged_at, observer_code, dome_code, result, note

The shipped report still reads the retired layout, so it comes back
empty.

dome_report_layout.md is the reporting rule the observatory board
agreed; the report closes on 2026-09-08.
initial_files.dome_report_layout.md:
Dome session report - Beacon Hill Observatory, v5 (2026-09-08)
=============================================================

The report is printed to standard output:

  domes with usable sessions: <number of listed domes>
  window: <first day>..<last day>
  <dome_code>,<usable_session_count>
  ... one line per listed dome ...

The reporting window is the 28 days ending on the report
date, counting both the first and the last day. This report closes
on 2026-09-08, so the window is 2026-08-12 through
2026-09-08, both dates included.

Which sessions count:
  - only sessions whose result is exactly `usable` count; aborted
    and clouded sessions never count, however long they ran;
  - only sessions logged inside the window count; a session logged
    before the window or after the report date belongs to another
    report and is left out.

Which domes are listed:
  - a dome is listed when at least one usable session inside the
    window was logged in it; a dome with none is left out, even if
    it logged sessions that did not count.

Ordering of the dome lines:
  - domes are listed by usable_session_count descending, busiest
    dome first;
  - domes sharing a count are listed by dome_code ascending.

Sessions are collected from every sessions-*.csv export under the
launch directory, no matter which folder an export sits in. The
observer_code and note columns are never printed.
initial_files.dome_report.py:
"""Dome session report for Beacon Hill Observatory.

Sweeps the log directory for sessions-*.csv exports and prints the
report to standard output.
"""
import csv
import glob
import os
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta

REPORT_END = date(2026, 9, 8)
WINDOW_DAYS = 28


def main() -> None:
    pattern = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "**", "sessions-*.csv")
    start = REPORT_END - timedelta(days=WINDOW_DAYS)
    counts = {}
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(pattern, recursive=True)):
        with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            for parts in csv.reader(handle):
                account, stamp, status = parts[0], parts[1], parts[2]
                if status != "usable":
                    continue
                day = datetime.fromisoformat(stamp).date()
                if not (start <= day <= REPORT_END):
                    continue
                counts[account] = counts.get(account, 0) + 1
    print("domes with usable sessions: %d" % len(counts))
    print("window: %s..%s" % (start.isoformat(), REPORT_END.isoformat()))
    for dome in sorted(counts):
        print("%s,%d" % (dome, counts[dome]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Dome session report for Beacon Hill Observatory.

Sweeps the launch directory for sessions-*.csv exports and prints
the report to standard output.
"""
import csv
import glob
import os
from datetime import date

REPORT_END = date(2026, 9, 8)
WINDOW_DAYS = 28
WINDOW_START = date(2026, 8, 12)


def main() -> None:
    pattern = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "**", "sessions-*.csv")
    counts = {}
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(pattern, recursive=True)):
        with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            for row in csv.DictReader(handle):
                if row["result"] != "usable":
                    continue
                day = date.fromisoformat(row["logged_at"][:10])
                if not (WINDOW_START <= day <= REPORT_END):
                    continue

initial_files.ranking_rules.md:
Gauge ranking - Kestrel Ridge Weather Station, rules v2 (2026-09-30)
==================================================================

The watch list is printed to standard output:

  gauge_id,total_mm
  ... one line per listed gauge ...

A monthly gauge export carries, in this order:

  gauge_id, reading_mm, recorded_at, flag

flag is ok or estimated. An estimated reading is a desk estimate,
not a measurement, and never counts towards a total.

How a gauge total is built:
  - every ok reading adds its reading_mm to its gauge's total;
  - a gauge with no ok reading has no total and is never listed.

Which gauges are listed (the wet-weather watch list):
  - first rank every gauge that has a total, wettest first; gauges
    sharing a total are ranked by gauge_id ascending;
  - the list is the three highest-ranked gauges; when further
    gauges share the total of the third-ranked gauge they are
    listed too, so the table can carry more than three lines.

Exports are collected from every gauges-*.csv file under the launch
directory, no matter which folder an export sits in. reading_mm and
total_mm are whole millimetres.

"""Gauge ranking for Kestrel Ridge Weather Station.

Sweeps the launch directory for gauges-*.csv exports and prints
the wet-weather watch list to standard output.
"""
import csv
import glob
import os


def main() -> None:
    pattern = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "**", "gauges-*.csv")
    totals = {}
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(pattern, recursive=True)):
        with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            for row in csv.DictReader(handle):
                if row["flag"] != "ok":
                    continue
                gauge = row["gauge_id"]
                totals[gauge] = totals.get(gauge, 0) + int(row["reading_mm"])
    ranked = sorted(totals.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0]))
    listed = ranked[:3]
    if listed:
        cutoff = listed[-1][1]
        listed = [item for item in ranked if item[1] >= cutoff]
    print("gauge_id,total_mm")
    for gauge, total in listed:
        print("%s,%d" % (gauge, total))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Bramley Vale Cider - press house intake
======================================

The scheduler launches the report as `python3 press_report.py` from
a scratch directory, never from the press house folder, so the

initial_files.press_layout.md:
Press intake totals - Bramley Vale Cider, spec v4 (2026-08-30)
=============================================================

The report is printed to standard output:

  orchard_code,net_litres
  ... one line per orchard ...
  total,<grand_total_litres>

An August extract carries, in this order:

  lot_ref, orchard_code, litres, unit, kind, state, variety, note

Against the retired lot_id, orchard, litres, type, status layout the
business fields were renamed and a unit column was inserted, and a
variety and a free-text note column were appended. note values may
contain commas and are then wrapped in double quotes, standard CSV.

How a lot counts towards the report:
  - only lots with state=accepted count; rejected lots never reach
    the report, whatever their kind;
  - kind=press adds litres to its orchard's figure; kind=return
    subtracts it. unit is always L and is never part of a figure.

Which orchards are listed:
  - every orchard with at least one accepted lot is listed, even
    when its net figure came out at exactly 0.

Ordering of the orchard lines:
  - orchards are listed by net_litres descending, largest first;
  - orchards sharing a net figure are listed by orchard_code
    ascending;
  - an orchard whose net figure is exactly 0 is listed after every
    other orchard, again by orchard_code ascending.

Extracts are collected from every pressings-*.csv file under the
launch directory, no matter which folder an extract sits in. The
grand total is the sum of the orchard lines printed above it.

initial_files.line_rules.md:
Line summary - Thornfield Bottling Plant, rules v3 (2026-09-01)
==============================================================

The summary is printed to standard output:

  line_code,net_bottles,best_day
  ... one line per listed line ...

A shift export carries, in this order:

  shift_ref, day, line_code, bottles, outcome

day is an ISO date. outcome is pass, breakage or void.

How a line's figure is built:
  - outcome=pass adds bottles to its line's figure;
  - outcome=breakage subtracts bottles from its line's figure;
  - outcome=void never counts, in either direction; a void shift is
    one the supervisor cancelled after its count was logged.

best_day is the day that contributed the largest daily net to its
line: a day's net is what that day's rows added or subtracted. Only
days carrying at least one counting row are considered, and when two
days are tied for the largest daily net the earlier day is the best
day. best_day is printed as an ISO date.

Which lines are listed:
  - every line carrying at least one counting row is listed, even
    when its net figure came out at exactly 0.

Ordering of the lines:
  - lines are listed by net_bottles descending, largest first;
  - lines sharing a net figure are listed by line_code ascending;
  - a line whose net figure is exactly 0 is listed after every other
    line, again by line_code ascending.

Exports are collected from every shifts-*.csv file under the launch
directory, no matter which folder an export sits in. shift_ref is for
the plant office only and is never printed.

arguments.content:
"""Per-line production summary for Thornfield Bottling Plant.

Sweeps the launch directory for shifts-*.csv exports and prints
the per-line figures to standard output.
"""
import csv
import glob
import os


def main() -> None:
    pattern = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "**", "shifts-*.csv")
    net = {}
    daily = {}
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(pattern, recursive=True)):
        with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            for row in csv.DictReader(handle):
                outcome = row["outcome"]
                if outcome == "void":
                    continue
                amount = int(row["bottles"])
                if outcome == "breakage":
                    amount = -amount
                line = row["line_code"]
                net[line] = net.get(line, 0) + amount
                per_day = daily.setdefault(line, {})
                per_day[row["day"]] = per_day.get(row["day"], 0) + amount
    listed = []
    for line, amount in net.items():
        best = min(daily[line].items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0]))
        listed.append((line, amount, best[0]))
    listed.sort(key=lambda item: (item[1] == 0, -item[1], item[0]))
    print("line_code,net_bottles,best_day")
    for line, amount, day in listed:
        print("%s,%d,%s" % (line, amount, day))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

One row per billing line. A shipment is identified by the pair (waybill,

web_fixture.content:
# Wrenfield flush tuning in the field

*Posted 2026-01-19 by R. Talviste, Edgefolk operators*

Our fleet ran Wrenfield 4.6 on roughly 900 edge boxes last winter; these notes are all from the 4.x series.

## Flush cadence

Out of the box, 4.x ships `flush_interval_ms` at 2000, so at most two seconds of telemetry is held before a flush. On metered links we raised it to 5000 and stopped paying for half-empty batches.

## Spool

We keep 15 minutes of local spool and let the shipper drop oldest-first once it is full.

*The 5.x rewrite replaced the shipper internals and its defaults; everything above reflects 4.x.*

web_fixture.title: Wrenfield 5.2 release notes
web_fixture.snippet: Release notes for Wrenfield 5.2: the shipper rewrite, and which engine the release ships its defaults from.
web_fixture.content:
# Wrenfield 5.2 release notes

Released 2026-06-30.

## Shipped defaults

5.2 completes the shipper rewrite begun in 5.0. The default flush cadence is no longer listed on this page: every interval and buffer setting is inherited from the engine the release ships with. 5.2 ships the **lantern** engine. The retired **kettle** engine is kept only for the 4.x series.

The engine reference lists the shipped default of each engine. A fresh 5.2 install never writes `flush_interval_ms` into `wrenfield.toml`, so the engine default is what runs.

## Other changes

- Spool files are now per-partition.
- `wrenfield doctor` reports the effective engine and every inherited default.

web_fixture.snippet: The shipped default of every inherited setting, listed per delivery engine.
web_fixture.content:
# Engine reference

Wrenfield 5.x delegates delivery to one engine per install, and each engine keeps its own shipped default for the inherited settings.

## flush_interval_ms

| Engine | Default |
| --- | --- |
| lantern | 750 |
| kettle | 2000 |

`lantern` flushes per partition and batches on a finer cadence; `kettle` is the legacy engine and keeps the value the 4.x series shipped.

## Other inherited settings

| Setting | lantern | kettle |
| --- | --- | --- |
| spool_max_mb | 640 | 512 |
| report_timeout_ms | 12000 | 9000 |

Last reviewed 2026-07-04.

web_fixture.content:
# Marlbrook checkpoint notes from a year in production

*Posted 2025-09-23 by D. Ferreira, Lanternpeer platform team*

We have run marlbrook 2.6 behind a Kafka ingest since early 2025. Two numbers shaped our SLO review.

## Checkpoint cadence

2.6 checkpoints every 120 seconds by default. On our feed of 11,000 events/second that meant a crash could cost us up to 1,320,000 events, so we tightened the cadence to 30 seconds for the payment topics.

## Sizing

Two cores per mutator pod held up well at that rate, and we never touched the sink batching.

*Written against marlbrook 2.6; the 3.x series reworked the checkpoint path.*

Release notes for marlbrook. Dates are release days.

- `marlbrook verify-wal` now reports the uncheckpointed window in events as well as in seconds.

## 4.0.0 (2026-02-03)

## 3.6.0 (2025-12-09)

- Checkpoint path reworked ahead of 4.0.

# Hollowbrook 3.8 release notes

Released 2026-08-04.

## Rollup defaults

The default `rollup_window` is now 1.4 seconds, down from the 1.8 seconds the earlier 3.x releases shipped and well below the 2.5 seconds of the 2.x line. The setting is still expressed in seconds, exactly like every other duration in `hollowbrook.toml`.

Nothing else in the rollup path changed, so a stock 3.8 install keeps the shipped window unless an operator overrides it.

## Other changes

- `hollowbrook doctor` gained a `--json` flag.
- The daemon exposes rollup counters on the admin socket.

# doctor command reference - Hollowbrook documentation

`hollowbrook doctor` validates a configuration file and prints every effective setting with the value the daemon would actually use.

## Durations

Every duration setting is printed in **milliseconds**, whatever unit the configuration file used. A three-second rollup window is therefore printed as 3000, and an operator reading the report never has to convert units by hand.

## Example

```
rollup_window          3000
spool_max_age         900000
report_timeout_ms       4000
```

Last reviewed 2026-08-12.

# relay settings

*fernwick documentation, 3.0 series*

The relay reads its settings from `relay.toml`. Every key below is optional and falls back to the shipped default in the table.

| Key | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

web_fixture.title: Sizing gravelrun for a nightly backlog

web_fixture.content:
# Sizing gravelrun for a nightly backlog

*Posted 2025-10-08 by P. Nkemelu, Batchworks engineering blog*

We have run gravelrun 5.x on the settlement backlog since the spring: four scheduler nodes, one shared queue.

## Slot budget

5.x reserves 32 worker slots per scheduler node out of the box. On our 5.x nodes that left plenty of headroom, and we only raised it when a single tenant started monopolising slots.

## What we would change

Nothing about the slots. The queue partitioning mattered far more than the slot count.

*Notes are from the 5.x series; gravelrun 6.0 reworked the pools.*

web_fixture.title: Gravelrun 6.0 release notes
web_fixture.snippet: Release notes for gravelrun 6.0: the reworked scheduler, its slot defaults, and the new pools.
web_fixture.content:
# Gravelrun 6.0 release notes

Released 2026-07-16.

## Slot defaults

6.0 raises the default `worker_slots` to 48 per scheduler node, up from the 32 that the 5.x series reserved. The reworked scheduler keeps more work in flight per node without extra CPU, so the shipped value moved up rather than down.

The per-node value is what `gravelrun status` reports; a deployment that pins `worker_slots` in `gravelrun.toml` overrides it per node.

## Pools

6.0 splits a deployment into a primary pool and a spillover pool. Pool membership does not change the per-node slot default.

web_fixture.title: Reference topology - gravelrun documentation
web_fixture.snippet: The node layout the install guide provisions for a default gravelrun 6.0 deployment.
web_fixture.content:
# Reference topology

The reference gravelrun 6.0 topology is the layout the install guide provisions when no topology file is supplied.

## Shape

The reference 6.0 topology runs five scheduler nodes: three in the primary pool and two in the spillover pool. All five are sized identically and all five run the shipped settings.

## Scaling

Add spillover nodes when the primary pool saturates; every added node takes the same per-node defaults.

Last reviewed 2026-07-30.

web_fixture.title: Storage layout - stonebow manual
web_fixture.snippet: How stonebow seals and retires log segments, and which storage settings control the layout.
web_fixture.content:
# Storage layout

*stonebow manual, 4.x series*

stonebow keeps a log of segments on local disk, and the storage settings decide how large a segment grows before it is sealed.

## Sealing

A segment is sealed once it reaches `segment_target_mb`. The 4.x series writes 256 MB segments by default, and a sealed segment is never appended to again.

## Retention

Sealed segments are removed by the retention job, so retention is measured in hours rather than in segments.

Shipped storage defaults are revised with every major series; check the release notes of the series you actually run.

web_fixture.title: stonebow 5.1 release notes
web_fixture.snippet: Release notes for stonebow 5.1: the storage defaults this release ships and the smaller changes.
web_fixture.content:
# stonebow 5.1 release notes

Released 2026-06-21.

## Storage defaults

5.1 raises the default `segment_target_mb` to 512, up from the 256 that the 4.x series wrote and the 128 of the 3.x line. The 5.x compaction path reads larger segments more efficiently, so the shipped value grew with the rewrite.

A deployment that pins `segment_target_mb` in `stonebow.toml` keeps its pinned value; the shipped default applies to fresh installs.

## Other changes

- `stonebow fsck` now reports per-segment checksums.

*A community note, last checked 2026-02-17*

We have tracked stonebow's shipped segment size across three majors.

| Series | Shipped segment_target_mb |

| 1.x | 64 |
| 2.x | 128 |
| 3.x | 128 |

The original 64 MB layout is where most of the old tuning advice comes from. We have not re-measured anything since the 5.x rewrite landed, so read the table as history rather than as the value a new install uses.
